title: Final review of the Phase 1 diff
description:
Review the full epic diff. Three things specific to this phase:

1. THE NEGATIVE ACCEPTANCE IS THE POINT. This epic's whole thesis is that ticks needs NO new public Go surface. Verify the diff promotes nothing out of internal/ and adds no exported API for the factory's benefit. If it did, the phase failed even if every test passes.

2. NO SUBPROCESS IN A LOOP. Check every new tk invocation site. One batched 'tk list --json' is correct; a call per tick is the failure mode. Measured fact for context: the dashboard refreshes every 2s but reads the factory's HTTP API, not the tracker — so nothing should have appeared in a render loop.

3. EXIT-CODE FIDELITY. The tracker reads moved from in-process to subprocess. Confirm a missing epic still exits ExitNotFound and a non-epic still exits ExitGeneric, and that a tk-not-found or tk-crashed case produces something a human can act on rather than a bare non-zero.

Route findings as new ticks under 3j4 rather than fixing inline unless trivial.
acceptance_criteria: The full diff is reviewed and every finding fixed or filed. Confirmed in writing: nothing left internal/, no new exported API exists for the factory, and no tk call sits in a loop. Exit-code fidelity verified against the pre-existing tests. go test ./... green.
closed_reason:
Completed: full epic diff reviewed against origin/main, with the reviewer verifying rather than trusting — it ran go build / go vet / go test ./... itself (all exit 0) and MUTATION-TESTED the load-bearing claims instead of reading them.

VERDICT ON THE THREE PRIORITY ITEMS:

1. NEGATIVE ACCEPTANCE — PASS. The diff has zero delete and zero rename entries outside .tick/; nothing was promoted out of internal/ and the exported surface actually SHRANK (DefaultHarnessBytes became unexported). Every new exported identifier is inside internal/ and therefore unreachable from an external module.

2. NO SUBPROCESS IN A LOOP — PASS. The only two tk invocation sites are both inside cloudReadTracker, each caller invokes it once, and all per-tick work runs against the in-memory map from the single list. The counter test was checked for vacuity and is not vacuous: five descendants, asserts exactly 2 calls, and separately asserts all five read back, so it cannot pass by the tracker doing less work.

3. EXIT-CODE FIDELITY — PASS on behaviour, GAP on coverage. Filed as p41. The mapping is correct by reading; no pre-existing test asserts it, which means my review brief was itself wrong to say 'verify against the pre-existing tests'.

MUTATION EVIDENCE: --all was removed on purpose and two tests failed loudly; reverted, tree clean. The reviewer also confirmed the dashboard wire struct field-for-field against cloud/factory/src/run-room.ts:301-319 (including the enum values), and compared the collect copies line by line against source — byte-identical, no divergence introduced by the copy.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE RECORD:
- 'Zero test files edited' was partially inaccurate: two dashboard test files WERE edited (mechanical renames plus the key-parity change). True where it matters — zero test files under cmd/tk/cmd were modified.
- The epic's acceptance criterion was FALSE as literally written, because internal/factory imports internal/gatewaytrace. The code is right and the criterion was imprecise: gatewaytrace and cloud/state are the factory's own packages and move to ticfac, so that edge survives the move by design. Criterion and repo-wiki/factory-ticks-boundary.md both corrected.

JUDGEMENT CALLS ASSESSED AND UPHELD: os.Executable()-then-PATH (right, with a documented residual when the binary is renamed or under go run); DefaultHarnessBytes duplicated rather than shared (right, and net-smaller exported surface — no test forces them equal, correctly, since they are allowed to diverge); the frozen herd key literal (acceptable, the weakest point in the diff, and correctly labelled as such at its site rather than papered over).
